Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Why would a holy book ask for evidence?

The Quran says 'bring your proof' to others and its own. Why would a scripture do that, and what does it ask?

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ لَن يَدْخُلَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَن كَانَ هُودًا أَوْ نَصَـٰرَىٰ ۗ تِلْكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمْ ۗ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَـٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is [merely] their wishful thinking. Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:111

Translation

Don’t trust in lying words, saying, ‘Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, are these.’

Original · Hebrew

אַל־תִּבְטְח֣וּ לָכֶ֔ם אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַשֶּׁ֖קֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה הֵֽמָּה׃

Jeremiah · 7:4

World English Bible

This may be unexpected. Many people assume religious claims can only be defended by tradition, authority or warning. In this verse, a claim that Paradise belongs to one group alone is answered neither with a threat nor with a rival claim. It is answered with a demand: bring your proof, if you are truthful. Note what that assumes: a claim about God is the kind of claim that can be asked for evidence. A book that thought faith needed none would have no reason to say this.

A question for you

What do you expect a religion to say when it is asked for evidence?

If you sayJust believe.
ThenMany people have heard that. It is not what this sentence says, and you can hold it to that.
If you sayHere is our tradition.
ThenTradition may be worth much. But the third part looks at a sentence that does not accept it as enough.
If you sayHere are our reasons.
ThenThen you are asking the same of every religion, and this page has to meet it too.

Part 2 of 3

﴿أَمَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَنۢبَتْنَا بِهِۦ حَدَآئِقَ ذَاتَ بَهْجَةٍ مَّا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُنۢبِتُوا۟ شَجَرَهَآ ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ يَعْدِلُونَ٦٠ أَمَّن جَعَلَ ٱلْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَجَعَلَ خِلَـٰلَهَآ أَنْهَـٰرًا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَٰسِىَ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ حَاجِزًا ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ٦١ أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ٦٢ أَمَّن يَهْدِيكُمْ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَمَن يُرْسِلُ ٱلرِّيَـٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦٓ ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ تَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ٦٣ أَمَّن يَبْدَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَمَن يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ أَءِلَـٰهٌ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِ ۚ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَـٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ٦٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

[More precisely], is He [not best] who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you rain from the sky, causing to grow thereby gardens of joyful beauty which you could not [otherwise] have grown the trees thereof? Is there a deity with Allāh?[1083] [No], but they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him]. Is He [not best] who made the earth a stable ground and placed within it rivers and made for it firmly set mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a deity with Allāh? [No], but most of them do not know. Is He [not best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth?[1084] Is there a deity with Allāh? Little do you remember. Is He [not best] who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a deity with Allāh? High is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him. Is He [not best] who begins creation and then repeats it and who provides for you from the heaven and earth? Is there a deity with Allāh? Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."

Translator's notes

[1083] Three meanings are implied: "Is there another god who did all of this with Allāh?" or "Is there any deity worthy to be worshipped along with Allāh?" or "Is there a deity to be compared with Allāh?"

[1084] Generation after generation.

Quran · An-Naml 27:60-64

Translation

For who is God, except Yahweh? Who is a rock, besides our God,

Original · Hebrew

כִּ֤י מִ֣י אֱ֭לוֹהַּ מִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וּמִ֥י צ֝֗וּר זוּלָתִ֥י אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

the Psalms · 18:31

World English Bible

Anyone can demand proof from others. What does this book offer? This passage closes a series of questions. Who made the heavens and the earth? Who sends the rain? Who answers someone in distress? Who guides you in the dark? Only then does it say: bring your proof. Its evidence is the world and your own experience. You may think that falls short. But it does not ask you to accept a claim because it is written. It points outside itself, at things you can look at.

A question for you

Is pointing at the world real evidence, in your view?

If you sayYes, for someone who is looking.
ThenThen the looking is part of the evidence for you. It remains to ask how to tell what you see from what you want to see.
If you sayNo. Nature needs no author.
ThenThat is the main rival account, and it owes as much defence as the other.
If you sayIt is a start, but not enough.
ThenA fair verdict. The signs give something only if they add up, if they do.

Part 3 of 3

﴿لَّيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ وَلَآ أَمَانِىِّ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ ۗ مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوٓءًا يُجْزَ بِهِۦ وَلَا يَجِدْ لَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

“I, Yahweh, search the mind. I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”

אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה חֹקֵ֥ר לֵ֖ב בֹּחֵ֣ן כְּלָי֑וֹת וְלָתֵ֤ת לְאִישׁ֙ כִּדְרָכָ֔יו כִּפְרִ֖י מַעֲלָלָֽיו׃

Jeremiah · 17:10

World English Bible

﴿قَـٰلَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُم بِأَهْدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمْ عَلَيْهِ ءَابَآءَكُمْ ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِۦ كَـٰفِرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[Each warner] said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that [religion] upon which you found your fathers?" They said, "Indeed we, in that with which you were sent, are disbelievers."

Quran · Az-Zukhruf 43:24

Translation

Yahweh, my strength, my stronghold, and my refuge in the day of affliction, the nations will come to you from the ends of the earth, and will say, “Our fathers have inherited nothing but lies, vanity and things in which there is no profit. Should a man make to himself gods which yet are no gods?”

Original · Hebrew

יְהוָ֞ה עֻזִּ֧י וּמָעֻזִּ֛י וּמְנוּסִ֖י בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה אֵלֶ֗יךָ גּוֹיִ֤ם יָבֹ֨אוּ֙ מֵֽאַפְסֵי־אָ֔רֶץ וְיֹאמְר֗וּ אַךְ־שֶׁ֨קֶר֙ נָחֲל֣וּ אֲבוֹתֵ֔ינוּ הֶ֖בֶל וְאֵֽין־בָּ֥ם מוֹעִֽיל׃ הֲיַעֲשֶׂה־לּ֥וֹ אָדָ֖ם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְהֵ֖מָּה לֹ֥א אֱלֹהִֽים׃

Jeremiah · 16:19-20

World English Bible

Here it becomes uncomfortable for everyone. The demand does not stop at other people. This verse tells Muslims that their wishes decide nothing, any more than anyone else's do. Nor does it help to say this is what my parents believed. The text records that reply, and a messenger answers with a question: what if I brought you better guidance than what you found your fathers on? So a person raised in faith owes the same honesty as a person raised outside it.

A question for you

If someone asked why you believe what you believe, what would the honest answer be?

If you sayI was raised in it.
ThenThere is no shame in that. It is where most people start. It is not yet a reason.
If you sayI have looked into it.
ThenThen you can say what would change your mind.
If you sayI believe very little, and I have my reasons.
ThenThen the same question applies to your reasons, and that is a fair test of them.

The same in the other books
